record.paper_title: Padua points and “fake” nodes for polynomial approximation: old, new and open problems
record.original_question: Can Padua points be extended from the square [-1,1]^2 to higher-dimensional hypercubes [-1,1]^d for d≥3? A self-contained solution should produce higher-dimensional analogues of the known two-dimensional Padua nodes: explicit node sets for total-degree polynomial interpolation with comparable stability properties.

evidence.quote: We do not know the Padua points on [−1, 1]^d, d ≥ 3.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer $n\ge 0$, let $\Pi_n^d$ denote the space of real polynomials in $d$ variables of total degree at most $n$, so that $\dim\Pi_n^d=\binom{n+d}{d}$. A finite set $X\subset[-1,1]^d$ with $|X|=\dim\Pi_n^d$ is called unisolvent for total-degree interpolation of degree $n$ if the Lagrange interpolation problem at $X$ has a unique solution in $\Pi_n^d$; its Lebesgue constant is
$$\Lambda_n(X)=\max_{x\in[-1,1]^d}\sum_{\xi\in X}|\ell_\xi(x)|,$$
where $\{\ell_\xi\}_{\xi\in X}\subset\Pi_n^d$ are the fundamental Lagrange polynomials at $X$.

In two dimensions, the Padua points of degree $n$ are an explicitly known family of unisolvent nodes on $[-1,1]^2$, arising as a self-intersecting Lissajous-type generating curve, whose Lebesgue constant grows like $O((\log n)^2)$ — the minimal possible order for total-degree polynomial interpolation on a planar compact set with nonempty interior.

Problem. For each integer $d\ge 3$, construct an explicit family of nodes $X_n\subset[-1,1]^d$ with $|X_n|=\binom{n+d}{d}$, unisolvent for total-degree interpolation in $\Pi_n^d$, whose Lebesgue constants satisfy
$$\Lambda_n(X_n)=O\!\bigl((\log n)^d\bigr)\quad\text{as }n\to\infty,$$
thereby providing a genuine higher-dimensional analogue of the Padua points (as opposed to tensor-product constructions that do not preserve the total-degree optimality). Equivalently, prove or disprove the existence of such an explicit node family on $[-1,1]^d$ for every $d\ge 3$.
artifact.status_search_result: The extension of Padua points from the square to hypercubes $[-1,1]^d$ for $d\ge 3$ is explicitly described as the biggest open problem in the area. In 3D only tensor-product constructions (e.g. Padua-based Weakly Admissible Meshes) are available, and no genuine total-degree analogue with optimal $O((\log n)^d)$ Lebesgue constant is known. No source found announcing a solution as of 2026.
